81: C is correct because Amazon SQS durably stores job items and decouples the producers from the processor nodes, satisfying the loose coupling and durable storage requirements, and an Auto Scaling group with a launch template scaling on the number of items in the SQS queue (target tracking on queue depth) adds and removes nodes in direct proportion to the work available. SQS guarantees jobs persist until processed, unlike SNS which is a fire-and-forget pub/sub service, and queue-depth scaling tracks actual workload better than CPU or network usage.
82: B is correct because an AWS Config rule can continuously evaluate certificates and flag any that will expire within 30 days as noncompliant, and an EventBridge rule that reacts to the Config compliance change can send a notification through SNS to the security team. ACM does not support user-defined notification rules, EventBridge has no native certificate expiration event, and this approach is fully managed and repeatable.
83: C is correct because Amazon CloudFront is a global CDN that caches content at European edge locations, so European users load the site from nearby edge caches while CloudFront fetches origin content from the on-premises servers, which satisfies the requirement that the backend remain in the United States. It can be deployed within days and requires no migration of the application.
84: B is correct because the production instances run 24 hours a day with steady, low utilization, which is the classic workload profile for Reserved Instances that provides a significant discount over On-Demand. The development and test instances run only 8 hours a day and will be stopped automatically when not in use, so On-Demand Instances are the most cost-effective choice for intermittent workloads, whereas Spot or Spot Blocks carry interruption risk that is inappropriate for these environments.
85: A is correct because S3 Object Lock in compliance or governance mode enforces write-once-read-many (WORM) protection, preventing objects from being modified or deleted by anyone, including the root account, for the retention period, which directly satisfies the regulatory requirement. S3 Versioning is a prerequisite for Object Lock and preserves all object versions, while lifecycle policies, ACLs, and EFS read-only mounts do not prevent privileged users from altering or deleting the data.
86: A is correct because AWS Secrets Manager is designed to store database credentials securely and can rotate them automatically on a schedule without code changes, satisfying the requirement to rotate user credentials frequently. The web servers retrieve the credentials at runtime through IAM permissions, so no long-lived credentials are embedded on the instances, unlike S3 buckets, files on the file system, or OpsCenter which is an incident management tool, not a secrets store.
87: D is correct because an SQS FIFO queue durably buffers the customer data events produced while the database is unavailable during an upgrade, so nothing is lost. A separate Lambda function polls the queue and writes to the database only when the upgrade completes, providing ordered, exactly-once processing; retry logic alone still loses data if the upgrade exceeds the runtime, and Lambda local storage is ephemeral.
88: A is correct because the Requester Pays feature on the company's S3 bucket makes the marketing firm, as the requester, pay the data transfer and request costs, keeping the company's own data transfer costs as low as possible. Cross-Region Replication or syncing to the firm's bucket would incur large ongoing replication and egress charges on the company's side, and cross-account access still leaves the transfer costs with the company.
89: A is correct because enabling S3 Versioning keeps every version of an object so an accidental deletion only adds a delete marker, and MFA Delete requires an MFA-authenticated request for any permanent deletion of versions, effectively preventing accidental or unauthorized deletion of the audit documents. It is the purpose-built S3 feature for this protection, whereas IAM MFA, lifecycle policies, or KMS encryption do not prevent deletion of the objects.
90: B is correct because a read replica offloads the random-interval reporting script's read queries to a separate instance, so the development team's workloads no longer contend with the script on the source database, and it requires only creating the replica and pointing the script at its endpoint. The Multi-AZ standby cannot serve read traffic, and manual exports or caching add more operational overhead.
91: A is correct because an S3 gateway endpoint is a free, horizontally scaled entry point in the VPC's route table that lets EC2 instances reach Amazon S3 over the AWS private network without traversing the internet, satisfying the security regulation. S3 buckets do not live in subnets, and a NAT gateway still sends traffic over the internet.
92: A is correct because a VPC gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 provides a private connection between the application tier in the VPC and S3 that stays entirely on the AWS network, so no traffic crosses the internet and no public credentials are needed. C is correct because a bucket policy that restricts access to only the application tier, for example by conditioning on the VPC endpoint, enforces least-privilege access to the sensitive data so no other sources can reach the bucket.
93: B is correct because Amazon Aurora MySQL with Aurora Replicas handles the heavy read activity with high availability and performance, and Aurora database cloning uses a copy-on-write protocol that creates a full, consistent copy of the production database in minutes regardless of size, so the development team gets the staging environment immediately without the export load that causes latency. mysqldump exports would recreate the same performance problem, and a Multi-AZ standby cannot be used for staging.
94: C is correct because S3 event notifications to SQS with a Lambda function consuming the queue is a fully serverless pipeline that processes each file immediately after upload and automatically scales from a few files to thousands with no servers to manage, giving the least operational overhead. Aurora and EMR add heavy infrastructure for a simple one-time transformation, and EC2 instances require ongoing management.
95: D is correct because read replicas with the same compute and storage resources as the source database can serve the read traffic with sufficient headroom and keep replication lag minimal, which optimizes performance immediately once the application is pointed at the replica endpoints. Smaller replicas would fall behind on replication and perform poorly, and a Multi-AZ standby is only for failover, not for serving reads.
96: C is correct because the IAM policy grants the ec2:TerminateInstances permission with a condition on the source IP of 10.100.100.254 and the us-east-1 Region, so users in the group can terminate an EC2 instance in us-east-1 only when their request originates from that IP address. The other options either misread the allow condition, the Region, or the direction of the effect.
97: D is correct because Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is a fully managed native Windows file system that provides SMB shares, is integrated with Active Directory for access control, and supports Multi-AZ deployment for high availability, which are exactly the requirements of a SharePoint workload. EFS uses NFS rather than SMB, S3 cannot be mounted as a Windows volume, and Storage Gateway is a hybrid caching service rather than a native HA shared storage service.
98: C is correct because duplicate Lambda invocations occur when the SQS visibility timeout expires before the function finishes, making the message visible again for another consumer to process. Increasing the visibility timeout to a value greater than the function timeout plus the batch window timeout ensures a message is not redelivered while it is still being processed, which is a queue configuration change with the least operational overhead.
99: D is correct because Amazon FSx for Lustre is a fully managed high-performance file system that natively supports Lustre clients, so the on-premises application servers can mount it directly, and it can optionally link to an S3 data repository. The other options either are not fully managed, do not support the Lustre protocol, or describe capabilities that EFS does not have.
100: C is correct because a KMS customer managed key lets the EC2 instance role perform encryption and decryption of the certificates in near real time through the AWS managed KMS API with fine-grained IAM control, and storing the encrypted data on Amazon S3 provides highly available, durable storage. Secrets Manager with manual updates adds operational overhead, a custom Lambda function is more work and less secure, and EBS volumes are tied to a single instance and Availability Zone rather than being as highly available.
